design.question: Within real 5-round pairs, is the rank association between the bound network's output N and the average-key-rank score D greater than, smaller than, or practically equal to its rank association with the CE2 single-trail probability T?
design.why: G-CE2 (median Spearman 0.807 between N and T, 20/20 positive) excludes the registered alternatives of CE2 but not a distributional account: Benamira et al. build a key-averaged distinguisher from a masked difference distribution that closely matches the network's 5-round accuracy. CE5 tests which registered account agrees better with the fixed network.
design.hypotheses_wording: Both D and T are differential-cryptanalytic quantities. CE5 compares two cryptanalytic explanations of the network's score; it does not test whether the signal is cryptographic, a result favouring one account does not disprove the other, and no outcome establishes a causal mechanism.

model.provenance: output of the authors' re-execution of Gohr's train_nets.py (depth 10, 5 rounds, 200 epochs), commit 2b54425; not Gohr's released weights

cipher.name: SPECK32/64
cipher.conventions: audit.cryptography.gohr.speck (Gohr's code); word order (l, r); MSB-first encoding

trail_proxy_T.source: audit.cryptography.ce234.production.generate_theory_data(n, with_factors=True), imported unmodified: product of the per-round xdp+ factors of the realised trail
trail_proxy_T.domain: real pairs only: T needs the realised intermediate differences, which a random pair does not have; the primary comparison is therefore conditional on real pairs
trail_proxy_T.persisted: T and the per-round factors F; the verifier checks T = prod(F) for feasible pairs

baseline_D.construction: average-key-rank differential distinguisher, Benamira et al. 2021, Sect. 4.5, Supplementary Algorithm 1 (aDDT construction) and Algorithm 2 (distinguisher), Table 7
baseline_D.algorithm_source_text_rule: Algorithms 1 and 2 transcribed verbatim with page numbers into docs/SOURCE_VERIFICATION.md; every step of akr.py and reference.py is mapped to a line of that transcription
baseline_D.source_location: P1 Sect. 4.5 pp. 17-18 (method, n = 10^7, mask, complexity); Supplementary A p. 32 (Algorithms 1 and 2); Table 7 p. 19
baseline_D.mask_applies_to: (dl || dv): 0xff8f on dl, 0xff8f on dv (Algorithm 1 L11)
baseline_D.table_definition: Algorithm 1: dl = l xor l', dv = l xor r xor l' xor r' at nr - 1 rounds; aDDT[(dl || dv) & m] += 1/n; stored as integer counts over the 2^26 masked cells
baseline_D.candidates: Algorithm 2 L4: key = 0 .. 2^12 - 1, literal; one-round decryption of both ciphertexts per candidate
baseline_D.lookup: aDDT[(dl || dv) & m]; Algorithm 2 L9 omits '& m', read as the masked cell written by Algorithm 1 L11 (interpretation recorded in docs/SOURCE_VERIFICATION.md)
baseline_D.score: score / 2^12 (Algorithm 2 L11), continuous, pre-threshold, kept for the correlations
baseline_D.decision: real iff score / 2^12 > 2^-HW(m) = 2^-26, strict (Algorithm 2 L11); used by the gate
baseline_D.smoothing: none: Algorithm 1 L2 initialises to zero and unseen cells contribute 0
baseline_D.table_check: an independent 10^5-pair sample from reference.py (own SPECK, own random stream) is compared with the recorded table over its 200 most frequent cells with expected count >= 5 plus a pooled remainder; PASS iff chi-square p >= 0.001 at the registered rounds and p < 1e-12 at one round fewer and one more

secondary_comparator_LR.construction: Algorithm 1 table at nr = 5 rounds (10^7 pairs, independent of the aKR table), read at the masked (dl || dv) of the ciphertexts themselves, no key guessing; secondary, not a published distinguisher

design.instrument_order: tables are built once, hashed and recorded here before calibration; calibration, gate and production all use the recorded tables
design.superseded: design r2 (2^13-class average of all 2^16 subkeys, (delta_l, delta_r) table) is kept in historical/r2_superseded_20261105 and is not evidence for this design
not_run: M-ODT/LightGBM (its masks are derived from the network, so it is not an independent baseline)

gate.purpose: the baseline must reproduce the published aKR result, not merely beat the DDT, before any confirmatory data exist
gate.published_ddt_location: P1 Table 1, p. 9, row D5 (0.911, 0.877, 0.947; taken from Table 2 of Gohr 2019); also P1 Table 10, p. 27
gate.published_evaluation_size: not stated for Table 7; Table 8 (p. 19) uses 10^5 pairs, about 50,000 per class
gate.table_variability: before approval, non-confirmatory: 5 independent tables built from fresh data, each scored on its own fresh 10^5 + 10^5 pairs; sigma_t = SD of the 5 accuracies (and of TPR, TNR)
gate.tolerance_rule: tau = max(0.005, 3 * sigma_t) for accuracy and tau_rate = max(0.010, 3 * sigma_t(rate)) for TPR and TNR, fixed from table_variability before approval
gate.rule: REPRODUCED iff the Clopper-Pearson 95% interval of accuracy lies inside [0.9298 - tau, 0.9298 + tau] and the CP intervals of TPR and TNR lie inside their published values +- tau_rate. SEPARATED (reported) iff the accuracy CP lower limit exceeds (0.9298 + 0.911) / 2. CE5 proceeds only on REPRODUCED; SEPARATED without REPRODUCED is reported as an adequacy result and CE5 is UNADJUDICATED
gate.data: fresh pairs from os.urandom after approval, independent of the tables and of every replicate
gate.reported: accuracy, TPR, TNR, full confusion matrix, both gate components
gate.on_failure: CE5 is UNADJUDICATED and the failure is reported; no replicate is run and no substitute baseline is run under this design

replicate.unit: replicate (independent fresh data); never the pair
replicate.real_pairs_record: validation/benchmark.json (r3, 2026-11-05T11:16:06Z): 0.109 ms and 36.3 bytes per real pair, covering one real and one random pair (generation, inference, aKR and LR scoring); 1.8 h and 2.2 GB at R = 60; peak footprint 885 MB

rules.real_pairs_per_replicate: largest of 10^4, 3x10^4, 10^5, 3x10^5, 10^6 whose projected production time (trail generation, network inference and aKR scoring of real and random pairs, each measured by the benchmark) at the worst-case R = 60 is at most 12 hours on the registered machine and whose raw files at R = 60 fit in 10 GB; fixed before calibration
rules.n_replicates: smallest R in {20, 25, ..., 60} for which, under a normal model with SD equal to the 80% upper confidence bound of the calibration SD of Delta, P(EQUIVALENT | Delta = 0) >= 0.80, P(DISTRIBUTION_GREATER | Delta = 2m) >= 0.80 and P(TRAIL_GREATER | Delta = -2m) >= 0.80; 60 if none, with the shortfall reported
rules.calibration: 10 blinded replicates at the chosen pair count on fresh data, after the margin is fixed: only the spread of Delta is kept, its location and all correlations are discarded; never evidence. The SD used is the 80% upper confidence bound of max(sample SD, 1.4826 * MAD)

replicate.data: fresh per replicate from os.urandom; raw arrays persisted before analysis

primary.statistic: Delta_r = atanh(rho_s(N, D | real)) - atanh(rho_s(N, T | real)) on the same real pairs of replicate r, rho_s = Spearman with average ranks for ties
primary.dependence: the two correlations share N and the pairs; their dependence is absorbed by taking the paired difference within each replicate and inferring across independent replicates
primary.interval: distribution-free interval for the median of Delta_r from binomial order statistics, coverage >= 95% (95.9% at R = 20)
primary.margin_rationale: proposal only: on the Fisher-z scale, which roughly stabilises the variance of a correlation; at the G-CE2 level (rho = 0.807) 0.10 moves rho by about 0.03 and the squared rank association by about 0.05. Under the revised outcomes a DISTRIBUTION_GREATER or TRAIL_GREATER verdict needs the whole interval beyond the margin, so the margin is the smallest difference the experiment can certify. The operator sets the value before calibration; no data have informed it.

outcomes.DISTRIBUTION_GREATER: lower limit >= margin (a practically meaningful difference is demonstrated)
outcomes.EQUIVALENT: -margin < lower limit and upper limit < margin
outcomes.INCONCLUSIVE: otherwise; a non-significant difference is never read as equivalence, and a difference whose interval excludes 0 but crosses the margin is reported only as a direction (qualifier DIRECTION_D or DIRECTION_T), never as practically meaningful

secondary.resolution_matched: T takes few distinct values and D is nearly continuous, which caps rho(N, T) below rho(N, D) for reasons of resolution alone. Delta_matched_r uses D re-ranked with T's tie structure (D's order, T's tie groups) in place of D; same interval and outcomes, descriptive
secondary.margin_sensitivity: the primary outcome at each margin in primary.margin_sensitivity, descriptive
secondary.class_conditional: rho_s(N, D | real) and rho_s(N, D | random), descriptive; T is undefined for random pairs
secondary.lr_comparator: Delta_LR_r = atanh(rho_s(N, LR)) - atanh(rho_s(N, T)), same interval, descriptive

incremental_value.target: van der Waerden normal scores of N
incremental_value.features: normal scores of T and D, each with degree-3 polynomial terms; M_TD adds T*D
incremental_value.fit: ordinary least squares on the first half of each replicate's real pairs
incremental_value.loss: mean squared error on the second half; the same evaluation pairs for all three models
incremental_value.statistics: Delta_D = L(M_T) - L(M_TD); Delta_T = L(M_D) - L(M_TD)
incremental_value.test: exact two-sided sign test over replicates for each; Holm over the two
incremental_value.interpretation: predictive information about N beyond the competing predictor; not causal reliance or mechanism

design.anchoring: preregistration.json must have an OpenTimestamps proof preregistration.json.ots whose embedded SHA-256 equals the file's; production refuses otherwise
design.verification: verify.py consumes the raw files and the tables only. It recomputes table hashes, the table check, gate accuracy and confusion matrix, D for 32 random pairs per class per replicate with reference.py (literal 2^16 enumeration), T = prod(F), every correlation, Fisher transform, paired difference, interval, incremental value and decision, and optionally N for 256 pairs per replicate from the checkpoint. Any mismatch makes the certificate NOT_VERIFIED
design.exclusions: a replicate is re-drawn only after an infrastructure failure, kept in the log
design.environment_requirement: Python 3.11, TensorFlow 2.21, Keras 3, numpy 2.x, scipy 1.17, CPU
not_claimed: that the network computes D or T
that rejecting the single-trail account rejects cryptographic learning
anything about other checkpoints, rounds or input differences
